newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures ended slightly higher, supported by a positive U.S. bond market, although volume was the lowest for a session since December 26, 1995.
Traders said there was little else driving French bonds besides the U.S. market and that they did not expect the situation to change much before next year.
They said given the current subdued conditions the contract would have trouble breaching the 129 level. It traded between 128.72 and 128.86 on Monday. Volume was a paltry 14,631 lots.
The 10-year spread between German and French bonds remained steady at minus four basis points.
As expected the Bank of France left interest rates unchanged at its regular money market tender on Monday. March PIBOR remained steady at 96.69, again with little volume.
The franc was up at 3.3753 against the mark compared with 3.3770 late on Friday.

Analysts said French national statistics institute INSEE survey of businesses in December, due for release on Tuesday at 0745 GMT would be of minor interest as it would give some indication about prospects for the first quarter next year.
